1. Core Clinical Tension: A 14-year-old adolescent presents with a 7-month history of isolated, continuous right flank pain without systemic signs, fever, hematuria, or urinary symptoms. Ultrasonography reveals a septated cystic lesion with fine internal echoes in the perinephric and subcapsular space of the right kidney, but subsequent contrast-enhanced abdominal CT imaging is atypical and does not demonstrate the pathognomonic radiological signs of a parasitic cyst. This discordance creates a challenging clinical dilemma between a complex congenital renal cyst (Bosniak category), retroperitoneal cystic neoplasm, chronic perinephric hematoma/abscess, and an isolated extrapulmonary, extrahepatic hydatid cyst.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint is reached at initial outpatient clinical and cross-sectional radiological workup (physical examination, renal ultrasonography, contrast-enhanced CT of abdomen and pelvis, and screening chest CT), but stopping strictly prior to send-out parasitic serological titers (IgG antibody assays), surgical enucleation with scolicidal agents, and gross/histopathologic examination of cyst contents.
3. Differential Distinctions: Simple cortical cysts of the kidney are common and benign, but they are thin-walled, anechoic, and lack internal septations, debris, or subcapsular localization. Complex renal cystic neoplasms (such as cystic renal cell carcinoma or multilocular cystic nephroma) usually arise from the renal parenchyma, show enhancing thickened septa or solid nodular components on CT, and do not demonstrate fine internal acoustic layering ('hydatid sand') or high-titer specific antibodies. Extracranial/extrahepatic hydatid disease can mimic malignant or benign retroperitoneal cysts when daughter cysts are obscured on CT, making ultrasound-serology correlation essential.
case_prompt:
A 14-year-old girl presented for outpatient evaluation of persistent right flank pain of seven months' duration. The pain was described as constant, non-radiating, and localized. A comprehensive review of systems was negative for gross hematuria, dysuria, urinary frequency, fever, chills, fatigue, weight loss, or changes in appetite. Her past medical and surgical histories were unremarkable.

On physical examination, she was in no acute distress and her vital signs were completely normal. Abdominal examination was soft and non-distended, with mild localized tenderness elicited upon deep percussion in the right costovertebral and right flank region. There were no palpable masses, peritoneal signs, or peripheral edema.

Renal ultrasonography demonstrated a well-defined cystic mass measuring 25 x 46 x 60 mm located in the subcapsular and perinephric space of the right kidney, abutting the interpolar and lower pole regions; the cyst exhibited fine low-level internal echoes and discrete internal septations. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis confirmed a well-circumscribed retroperitoneal fluid collection in the right perinephric subspace, completely separate from the renal parenchyma, though the CT appearance lacked typical calcification or obvious internal daughter vesicles. A screening CT of the chest and review of hepatic parenchyma on abdominal imaging revealed no lung or liver lesions.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Complex Benign Renal Cyst / Bosniak Category IIF/III Cystic Mass
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the indolent presentation and presence of internal septations on sonography without constitutional symptoms, but ruled out because the subcapsular/perinephric location outside the parenchyma and specific fine internal echoes raised concern for an infectious etiology, later confirmed serologically and pathologically.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: In the sonography of the patient, a cystic lesion with a fine internal echo and septation with dimensions of 25 x 46 x 60 mm can be seen in the subcapsular and perinephric space of the right kidney in the vicinity of the middle and lower bridge of this kidney, which can indicate a hydatid cyst.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Cystic Renal Cell Carcinoma / Retroperitoneal Cystic Neoplasm
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the persistent unilateral pain and atypical CT findings that did not show typical characteristics of a hydatid cyst, but ruled out following positive serology and surgical exploration which confirmed a benign parasitic capsule with daughter cysts rather than malignant cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The interesting thing about this patient was that the patient's CT scan did not look very similar to a hydatid cyst, and the sonographer, based on the evidence in the ultrasound, suggested a differential diagnosis of a hydatid cyst for the patient.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point was established when specific hydatid IgG antibody serology returned positive at a titer of 1:160, followed by surgical extirpation with hypertonic saline scolicidal irrigation, which confirmed an intact subcapsular cyst containing characteristic daughter cysts on pathologic examination.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Hydatid IgG antibody titer of the patient was 1.160, which was considered positive.

editor_comments: Standardized admission diagnostic case following Stanford MedCaseReasoning. Breakpoint stops following ultrasound and CT imaging before serologic titers and surgical pathology. Zero spoilers in case_prompt. Candidates and Diagnostic Pivot supported by verbatim quotes.
